simple.meaning: עָמֵל (ʻâmêl) is a Hebrew object word meaning “toiling ; concretely, a laborer ; figuratively, sorrowful.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Judges 5:26. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָמֵל (H6001) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: עָמֵל (ʻâmêl) / H6001 is traced through Judges 5:26, Job 3:20, Job 20:22, Proverbs 16:26 with generated occurrence evidence.

structuredEvidence.definition: toiling ; concretely, a laborer ; figuratively, sorrowful

firstOccurrence.englishText: She put her hand to the tent peg,

timeline.evidenceText: She put her hand to the tent peg,
“Why is light given to him who is in misery,
In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress will overtake him.
The appetite of the laboring man labors for him;
I hated all my labor in which I labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
For what does a man have of all his labor and of the striving of his heart, in which he labors under the sun?
What profit has he who works in that in which he labors?

There is one who is alone, and he has neither son nor brother. There is no end to all of his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied with wealth. “For whom then, do I labor and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.

Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of your life of vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all your days of vanity, for that is your portion in life, and in your labor in which you labor under the sun.
